text:
Dear Ms. Santos,

I plan to build a two-bedroom, 1,100 square foot home on my lot in Pāhoa because I want a safe, simple place for my family. I have a full budget for land, permits and construction, and I chose a licensed contractor after comparing three bids and calling their references.

The builder estimates the project will take about ten months to complete. I know building often brings surprises, so I am keeping a contingency fund of ten percent for unexpected costs or delays.

Once the home is finished, my steady income as an electrician will cover the mortgage payment each month, and I will use autopay so it is always on time.

Thank you for considering my project.

Sincerely,
Keahi Kamaka

Dear Loan Officer,

I am requesting a construction loan to build a small three-bedroom home in Waimea. My family has outgrown our rental, and building lets us design a home that fits our needs and our budget.

I worked with a licensed builder on a detailed estimate. The total cost, including permits and site work, fits our plan, and the builder's schedule shows completion in about nine months. We have set aside an emergency cushion for delays and price increases.

After construction, our combined income easily covers the monthly mortgage payment. We have a record of paying every bill on time.

I appreciate your time and consideration.

Respectfully,
Roberto and Lani Silva

Dear Mr. Fujimoto,

I want to build a small house on my land because building costs less than buying here, and I can make it just right for my family.

I made a budget for the whole project. I picked a contractor who is licensed and had the best bid. The builder said it will take about eight months to finish.

I know things can go wrong, so I am saving extra money as a contingency fund in case of a delay or a surprise cost. After the house is built, I will pay the mortgage every month with my income from my job.

Thank you for reading my letter.

Mahalo,
Ikaika Lum

To the construction lending team,

Thank you for reviewing my application. I am building a one-story home in Hilo designed for my mother and me. A single floor will let her live with us safely as she gets older.

My budget includes the land, the build, permits and utilities. I interviewed several contractors and chose a licensed builder with a fixed-price bid and good references. The timeline is eleven months, and I will check on the work every week.

I am keeping a contingency fund for unexpected repairs and delays. When the home is complete, the mortgage payment will be less than our current rent, and my income as a nurse is steady.

Sincerely,
Mele Kauhane

Dear Loan Officer,

I want to build a three-bedroom house on my lot because my family needs more space. I have a budget and a licensed contractor. The builder says it will take about a year to finish.

After it is built, I will pay the mortgage on time every month with my income.

Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
Kevin Tran
